items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I ended up with George Shearing as the bass player in a permanent position... that was the beginning of the George Shearing Quintet... which was Denzel Best, Margie Hyams, Chuck Wayne, George Shearing and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah. You could see — you could probably see that it could be done a lot better.

Oh, yeah, and that really ticked me off because everything was backwards, you know. We didn’t get paid on time, and when you had to travel no arrangements were being made for it, and nothing. Everybody was on their own, you know, and I didn’t like it. So © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

when they left to go to California, I decided I was going to quit. So I left that group and this was about the time that I was just sort of like floating around. I got a call to come down to Birdland to work, finish out a week with Buddy Rich. Buddy Rich had a big band. So I went down to Birdland and worked the week with Buddy Rich and George Shearing was playing opposite Buddy Rich. In other words, in those days, in Birdland, there might be three or four different acts. And in this case I think it was George…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But anyway, he asked me to work with him until this guy came back. Fine. ... I started with Shearing.

ctx.x: Okay. And basically begin playing again at various clubs and spots?

Yeah. That’s all. Just whatever gigs came along. When I got the call which led to Shearing was from Jimmy Jones calling me to come and sit in with [the] Buddy Rich big band, which was working opposite Jimmy Jones and Sarah Vaughan’s group. George Shearing was in there also. This is the way it used to work. You had three or four different groups playing at a nightclub. At that time, this was Buddy Rich with a big band, Sarah Vaughan with her group, Shearing and Buddy DeFranco, all worked in the same place. We all…

items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: That’s because before the quintet even, Buddy DeFranco, John Levy on bass, Denzil Best on drums and me, before the quintet, in the Clique Club in New York

ctx.x: This was 1946. I was born in ‘19 so what was I, 27?
Then you met John Levy and the group, here.
John Levy, I met John Levy and the group, and John Levy did recording with me before, oh, well about the same time the quintet started. 1949.
